_meta.name: California K-12 School District GO Bond Universe
_meta.purpose: Universe scoping for ca_k12_dedicated_tax_special_revenue masking-mechanism validation. K-12 GO bonds are the largest CA muni sector by outstanding par (~$200B+ across 900+ districts). Hypothesis tested: does a state-apportionment intercept analogous to CSFA LCFF exist? Finding: NO state-apportionment intercept; the actual masking mechanism is the SB 222 (2016) statutory lien + Fitch / S&P / Moody's 'dedicated property tax = pledged special revenue' rating treatment, which permits dedicated-tax GO ratings up to 5 notches above the district's Issuer Default Rating (IDR).

key_structural_facts.fact_1_no_state_apportionment_intercept_: California K-12 school district GO bonds are NOT secured by state apportionment / Prop 98 / LCFF funding. Unlike CSFA charter conduit deals (Ed Code 17199.4 State Controller LCFF intercept), district GO bonds are secured SOLELY by ad valorem property taxes levied by the COUNTY on the district's tax roll. State apportionment money never touches the bond trustee. Sources: California Debt Financing Guide §B.1.3.1; Orrick 2015 SB 222 client alert.
key_structural_facts.fact_2_no_california_permanent_school_fu: California has NO bond-guarantee program analogous to Texas Permanent School Fund (PSF). Texas PSF guarantees ~$100B+ of TX school district bonds with AAA wrap from $60B+ fund corpus; CA has no parallel structure. The State Allocation Board (SAB) administers School Facility Program matching grants for state-bond-funded construction, but does NOT guarantee local district GO. Source: tea.texas.gov PSF disclosure; CA DGS OPSC bond oversight.
key_structural_facts.fact_3_ab_8_is_property_tax_allocation_n: AB 8 (1979) implemented Prop 13 by allocating reduced property tax revenues among local agencies (cities, counties, schools, special districts). Schools' share dropped from ~50% to ~36% of total property-tax base; state replaced shortfall via general fund. AB 8 is a HORIZONTAL allocation mechanism, NOT a bondholder pledge or intercept structure. ERAF (1992-93, 1993-94) reshuffled $3.6B from counties/cities back to schools but again is intra-government allocation, not bond security. Source: LAO 'Reconsidering AB 8' (2000); LAO 'Property Taxes: Why Some Local Governments Get More' (1996).
key_structural_facts.fact_4_sb_222_statutory_lien_is_the_mask: SB 222 (effective January 2016) codified an automatic statutory lien on the levy-and-collection of ad valorem property taxes pledged to pay K-12 / community college district GO bonds. The lien attaches at the moment of levy without further act, is binding on the district's successors and creditors, and was designed specifically to clarify special-revenue status under U.S. Bankruptcy Code § 902(2). California's existing statutory framework (Ed Code §15250 et seq., Gov't Code §53550) prohibits the use of property-tax bond-debt-service revenues for any operating purpose. Source: Cal. Gov't Code §53515 (added by SB 222 Ch. 932, 2015); Orrick 2015-03 alert.
key_structural_facts.fact_5_fitch_5_notch_uplift_criteria: Fitch's tax-supported rating criteria (2016 update) explicitly permits CA school district dedicated-tax GO bonds to be rated up to 5 NOTCHES above the district's Issuer Default Rating (IDR). Required criteria include: (1) explicit statutory prohibition on use of bond-tax revenues for operations, (2) bondholders solely secured by dedicated tax (no claim on general fund revenues), (3) automatic statutory lien (SB 222), (4) bankruptcy-code special-revenue treatment per legal opinion, (5) unlimited tax levy authority. Source: Bond Buyer 'California School GO Structure Seen as Special Revenues' (2016); Bond Buyer 'Fitch Signals Shift on California School GO Ratings'.
key_structural_facts.fact_6_sacramento_usd_is_load_bearing_an: Sacramento City USD (2026-04-28 Fitch action): IDR cut to BB- from A+; ULTGO (older series, no dedicated-tax pledged-special-revenue language) cut to BB- from A+; DEDICATED-TAX GO cut to BBB+ from AAA; LRB cut to B+ from A. The dedicated-tax GO retained EXACTLY 5 notches above IDR (BBB+ vs BB-), confirming the Fitch criteria cap. This is the single cleanest empirical anchor for the masking mechanism — proves it is PARTIAL not absolute (dedicated-tax GO did fall from AAA to BBB+ when IDR collapsed), but the 5-notch gap held. Source: Bond Buyer 'Sacramento school bonds downgraded to junk on fiscal woes' (April 2026).
key_structural_facts.fact_7_lausd_negative_idr_aaa_dedicated_: LAUSD (2026-04-20 Fitch action): IDR AA- affirmed but outlook revised to NEGATIVE; ULTGO AA- negative outlook; COPs A+ negative; DEDICATED-TAX GO AAA STABLE outlook (unchanged). Enrollment 389K vs 746K in 2002-03 = 48% decline; ADA erosion is severe operator-signal. Yet dedicated-tax GO held AAA stable. Cleanest demonstration that operator-signal does NOT propagate to dedicated-tax GO spread within the rating band. Source: Bond Buyer 'Los Angeles school bond outlook dropped to negative by Fitch, Moody's' (April 2026).
key_structural_facts.fact_8_state_emergency_loans_to_district: California Education Code §41320 et seq. provides for state emergency apportionment loans to insolvent districts. Vallejo USD ($60M loan 2004, repaid Aug 2024, exited receivership June 2025), Inglewood USD ($29M loan 2014, repayment through 2034-35), West Fresno, Oakland, Compton, Coachella, Emery — all received state loans. CRITICAL: emergency loans go to DISTRICT OPERATIONS, not to bondholders. Bondholders are paid by the COUNTY out of the dedicated property tax (which never enters district treasury). State receivership has ZERO direct credit-positive effect on bondholder cash flow; the bondholder is already protected by the dedicated-tax structure regardless of whether the state intervenes. Sources: Ed Code §41320.1; FCMAT 2024 Inglewood progress report.
key_structural_facts.fact_9_universe_size_outstanding_par: Total CA K-12 GO outstanding par estimated $150-200B across ~900 districts (CDIAC DebtWatch). LAUSD alone ~$11.8B post-2026 issuance (Moody's). Top-10 districts ~30-40% of par. Compares to CSFA charter universe of ~$3-5B (1-2% of K-12 GO size).
key_structural_facts.fact_10_voter_approval_55_threshold: Prop 39 (2000) reduced voter approval threshold from 2/3 to 55% for K-12 GO bonds meeting accountability requirements. Resulted in surge of district bond passage; failed-bond districts (those that ATTEMPTED but lost) are a separate distress signal (suggests local political opposition to tax base) and are typically rated lower.

universe_size_summary._methodology: Targeted 30-50 per task spec; 32 sampled across 5 strata. Universe not exhaustive; representative for masking-mechanism validation. Not pulled: Long Beach USD per-rating (just inferred AA category), San Marino USD (small district, likely AAA suburb but no recent Fitch report).

_meta.masking_mechanism_verdict_summary: VERIFIED — `ca_k12_dedicated_tax_special_revenue` masking mechanism EXISTS but is STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from CSFA LCFF intercept. It is NOT a state-apportionment intercept (no apportionment flows to bondholders); it IS a dedicated-property-tax + statutory-lien + bankruptcy-code-special-revenue carveout that creates a 5-notch ceiling between district IDR and dedicated-tax GO rating. The Sacramento USD 2026-04-28 action (IDR BB-, dedicated-tax GO BBB+, exactly 5 notches) and LAUSD 2026-04-20 action (IDR AA- negative, dedicated-tax GO AAA stable, 4 notches) provide the load-bearing empirical anchors. Mechanism is closer in structure to ROPS allocation intercept (property-tax waterfall carveout) than to CSFA LCFF intercept (state-money intercept).
